## Incident Report — Vidar Stealer Infection (2022-01-07 Exercise)

### 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 | Consistent source IP across all NBNS, Kerberos, and C2 traffic |
| MAC address | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 | ARP table and DHCP request bound to 192.168.1.216 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 | DHCP option 12 hostname; also NBNS name `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2` (same host, OCR/case variance in NBNS broadcast) |
| Logged-in user | steve.smith (domain: SPOONWATCH.NET) | Kerberos `CNameString` field on AS-REQ/TGS-REQ from 192.168.1.216 to DC 192.168.1.2 |

Domain controller for context: `SPOONWATCH-DC.spoonwatch.net` (192.168.1.2), confirmed via NBNS and LDAP RootDSE query in `tcp.stream 0`.

### 2. Malware Family

**Vidar Stealer** — attribution is **behavioral** (no AV/IDS signature file was present in this evidence set; identification is based on matching the well-documented Vidar TTP fingerprint):

- HTTP POST traffic to a bare IP (no corresponding DNS lookup for that IP anywhere in the capture — consistent with Vidar's practice of resolving its true C2 from a hardcoded profile page rather than direct DNS).
- Distinctive, non-browser HTTP headers on every request: `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`, `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16, *;q=0.1`, `Accept: text/html, application/xml;q=0.9, ... image/x-xbitmap, */*;q=0.1` — no `User-Agent` header at all. This exact header combination is a known Vidar client fingerprint.
- Sequential download of files named `1.jpg` through `7.jpg` from the C2 that are **not actually images** — `file` identifies them as Windows PE32 DLLs. Their embedded strings match the exact NSS/Mozilla/VC++ redistributable set Vidar fetches to parse browser credential stores: `freebl3.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `nssdbm3.dll`, `sqlite3.dll`, `mozglue`-related, `msvcp140.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll`.
- Final POST to `/osk/` uploads a file named `_5861695120.zip` (Content-Type: `zip`, disguised inside the `/osk/` path) whose internal directory structure is `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/` — the exact stolen-data folder layout Vidar produces (browser autofill data, credit-card data, cookies), each named per-browser (`Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `Google Chrome_Network.txt`).
- Prior POST to `/osk//main.php` returned `200 text/html` — consistent with a Vidar-style check-in/config-fetch step before the module downloads.

No initial infection vector (dropper, phishing document, or exploit) is present in this capture; the trace begins with the host already on the domain and the C2 conversation starting at t=203s. Delivery occurred outside the capture window.

### 3. Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in this capture)

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` — sole non-Microsoft, non-domain-resolved destination; hosts the entire Vidar POST/download session in `tcp.stream` starting at frame 1501.

**Malicious domain**
- None observed. The C2 IP is contacted directly with no preceding DNS query for it anywhere in the capture.

**Malicious URLs (all on 2.56.57.108)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (config/check-in, HTTP 200)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `.../7.jpg` (module downloads, each returned `image/jpeg` content-type but PE32 DLL content — HTTP 200 each)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (final exfil upload, POST body 379,629 bytes, `multipart/form-data`, HTTP 200)

**Transferred files / hashes (SHA-256, computed locally from exported objects)**

| File | Role | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `1(1).jpg` | Downloaded PE32 DLL (sqlite3.dll strings) | not independently listed above — see note |
| `osk` | Exfiltrated ZIP `_5861695120.zip` (autofill/cc/cookies theft) | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` |

Note: hashes for `1(1).jpg`–`7(1).jpg` (the disguised DLL downloads) were not captured in the shasum run above — only `osk` and the unrelated Windows Update `.cab`/`.exe` files were hashed. If needed for the report appendix, hash the seven `N(1).jpg` files directly; they are the actual Vidar module payloads.

**Benign context (exclude from IOC list)**
- All `*.windowsupdate.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `*.data.microsoft.com`, `bing.com`, `msn.com` traffic and their associated `.cab`/`am_delta_patch_*.exe` downloads are legitimate Windows Update / Microsoft Defender signature update traffic, unrelated to the infection.
- All LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/DCERPC/NBNS traffic to 192.168.1.2 (SPOONWATCH-DC) is normal AD domain member traffic.

### Summary

Windows workstation `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2` (192.168.1.216, MAC `9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9`), logged in as domain user `steve.smith` on `SPOONWATCH.NET`, was infected with Vidar Stealer. The malware checked in with its C2 at `2.56.57.108`, downloaded seven Vidar helper DLLs disguised as `.jpg` files to enable parsing of browser credential stores, then exfiltrated a ZIP archive of stolen browser autofill data, saved credit-card data, and cookies to the same C2 over plaintext HTTP.
